The son of immigrants from the Dominican Republic, Villanueva was raised in [[Elmhurst, Queens]], New York City. He was drafted at the age of 20 with the seventh overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He also holds Dominican citizenship and has represented the [[Dominican Republic men's national basketball team|Dominican Republic national team]] in international competitions.{{cite web|url=http://puertorico2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/facm/player/p/eid/4042/pid/49590/sid/4042/tid/274/profile.html|title=Charlie Villanueva Player Profile|access-date=November 27, 2010|publisher=[[FIBA]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213072221/http://puertorico2009.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/facm/player/p/eid/4042/pid/49590/sid/4042/tid/274/profile.html|archive-date=February 13, 2010|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/downloads/Regulations/170310_FIBA_Internal_Regulations.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101215052416/http://www.fiba.com/downloads/Regulations/170310_FIBA_Internal_Regulations.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 15, 2010|page=67|title=Internal Regulations 2010|publisher=[[FIBA]]}} ==Personal life== Villanueva has an autoimmune skin disease known as [[alopecia universalis]], a variation of [[alopecia areata]]. This prevents the growth of hair on the [[scalp]] and/or elsewhere on the body, but otherwise is not physically painful, dangerous, or life-threatening. Villanueva is a spokesman for the NAAF (National Alopecia Areata Foundation),[https://web.archive.org/web/20070927211643/http://www.naaf.org/Charlie/Charlie-Bio.asp Charlie Villanueva Biography] and received the February 2006 [[NBA Community Assist Award|Community Assist Award]] from the NBA for his work with the organization.[http://www.nba.com/community/caa_feb_060313.html?rss=true Villanueva Receives Community Assist Award for February] A first-generation Dominican-American, Villanueva is fluent in Spanish, as it is the language he speaks with his family.{{Cite web |url=http://charlievillanueva.com/aboutcharlie/ |title=The Story: Charlie Villanueva |access-date=February 10, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104095959/http://charlievillanueva.com/aboutcharlie/ |archive-date=January 4, 2015 |url-status=dead }} Villanueva has three brothers, all named Roberto, a.k.a. Rob, after their father's name: Rob Antonio, Rob Elia, Rob Carlos. Announced in September 2015, Villanueva is working with two of the three brothers on a documentary titled "What is Alopecia", in order to continue his advocacy efforts to educate, create awareness and support the alopecia community.[https://www.mavs.com/charlie-villanueva-sets-out-to-make-a-documentary-about-his-career-condition/ Charlie Villanueva sets out to make a documentary about his career, condition] Villanueva has two children from a first marriage.[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/mavs-charlie-villanueva-leaves-team-birth-2nd-child-002544691--nba.html Mavs' Charlie Villanueva leaves team for birth of 2nd child] Villanueva tied the knot a second time on July 24, 2021, in Dallas, Texas, after Villanueva proposed to Lala Alvarez on New Year’s Eve 2020 at Nick & Sam’s, a steakhouse where they had their very first date.{{Cite web | title=Charlie Villanueva shares photos from hit-and-run car accident | url=https://nypost.com/2023/12/29/sports/charlie-villanueva-shares-photos-from-hit-and-run-car-accident/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229140256/https://nypost.com/2023/12/29/sports/charlie-villanueva-shares-photos-from-hit-and-run-car-accident/ | access-date=2026-08-30 | archive-date=2023-12-29}} ==High school career== During his freshman year, Villanueva attended [[Newtown High School (Queens)|Newtown High School]] in [[Queens, New York]], where he was a teammate of future NBA player [[Smush Parker]]. He spent his next three years at [[Blair Academy]] in [[Blairstown, New Jersey]], where he played with another future NBA player, [[Luol Deng]]. Villanueva received [[All-American]] honors as a senior and was named New Jersey Co-Player of the Year. He entered the [[2003 NBA draft]], but withdrew his eligibility so he could play college basketball for the [[University of Connecticut]]. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Villanueva was listed as the No. 2 power forward and the No. 5 player in the nation in 2003.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Charlie-Villanueva-3518 Charlie Villanueva Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Villanueva originally gave a verbal commitment to play for the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]], but after [[Bill Self]] left the [[Illinois Fighting Illini|Illini]] for the [[University of Kansas]], Villanueva withdrew his commitment. He considered following Self to the [[Kansas Jayhawks|Jayhawks]], but instead opted to play for the [[University of Connecticut]].[http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2003/jun/20/villanueva_snubs_draft/ Villanueva snubs draft for UConn] In his freshman year at UConn, Villanueva earned [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Rookie Team honors and was a key reserve member of the [[2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2004 NCAA National Championship team]]. As a sophomore at UConn, he averaged 13.6 points and 8.3 rebounds, leading the team in scoring and receiving team [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] and second-team All-Big East honors. Villanueva declared for the [[2005 NBA draft]] following his sophomore season, thus forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2005–2006)=== Villanueva was selected by the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the seventh overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. Despite being panned by critics as soon as his name was called in the draft,[http://www.nba.com/awards2006/thecase_rookie_villanueva.html Making the Case For Rookie of the Year: Charlie Villanueva - Toronto Raptors] Villanueva responded with a solid rookie season. He averaged 13.0 points and 6.4 rebounds in 81 games. He finished second among rookies in points and rebounds, and third in minutes and blocked shots. He also tallied 12 double-doubles and set the Raptors' rookie records for points (48) and rebounds (18) in a game. He also appeared in the Rookie Challenge and was named to the All-NBA Rookie first team. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2006–2009)=== On June 30, 2006, Villanueva was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[T. J. Ford]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2506311 Raptors deal Villanueva to Bucks for Ford][https://toronto.citynews.ca/2006/07/01/raptors-trade-charlie-villanueva-for-guard-t-j-ford/ Raptors Trade Charlie Villanueva For Guard T.J. 38 points and made a career-high seven 3-point shots during a loss against his former team, the Raptors.[https://www.twincities.com/2008/04/09/bosh-has-32-points-11-rebounds-as-raptors-beat-bucks-111-93-to-end-three-game-losing-streak/ Bosh has 32 points, 11 rebounds as Raptors beat Bucks 111-93 to end three-game losing streak] In March 2009, Villanueva was reprimanded by Bucks coach [[Scott Skiles]] for posting a message on his [[Twitter]] account during halftime of the Bucks–[[Boston Celtics|Celtics]] game.[https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2009/03/17/nba_player_scolded_for_using_twitter_at_halftime.html NBA player scolded for using Twitter at halftime] Despite the mishap, Villanueva's 2008–09 season turned out to be a career-best season for him as he averaged 16.2 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/v/villach01/gamelog/2009/ Charlie Villanueva 2008-09 Game Log] On March 3, 2009, Villanueva scored 24 points and grabbed 15 rebounds during a loss to the [[New Jersey Nets]].[https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2009/03/03/NBA-New-Jersey-99-Milwaukee-95/70561236142528/ NBA: New Jersey 99, Milwaukee 95] ===Detroit Pistons (2009–2014)=== [[File:Charlie Villanueva 20090930-5521.jpg|thumb|Villanueva with the [[Detroit Pistons|Pistons]] in 2009]] On July 8, 2009, Villanueva signed a five-year, $40 million contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4314591|title=Pistons sign Gordon, Villanueva|publisher=ESPN|date=July 8, 2009|access-date=August 6, 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4301111|title=Sources: Gordon, Villanueva to Pistons|publisher=ESPN|date=July 2, 2009|access-date=August 6, 2015}} Villanueva had scored a career high 16.7 points per game with Milwaukee the previous season. He was described by Pistons President of Basketball Operations [[Joe Dumars]] as "a versatile big man who can play in the post and score from the perimeter as well." He and fellow Pistons signee [[Ben Gordon]] were described as "key pieces to our roster next season."{{cite web |title=Pistons Sign Free Agents Ben Gordon and Charlie Villanueva |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/gordon_villanueva_090708.html |website=Detroit Pistons |language=en}} In November 2010, Villanueva [[tweeted]] that [[Boston Celtics]] forward [[Kevin Garnett]], a known [[Trash-talk|trash-talker]], called him a "cancer patient" during a Celtics blowout win over Detroit. In response, Garnett insisted that "My comment to Charlie Villanueva was in fact 'You are cancerous to your team and our league,'" and that he meant no insult to those afflicted with cancer. Celtics coach [[Doc Rivers]] backed up Garnett's correction.{{cite news |title=Tweet says KG called Villanueva 'cancer patient' |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/news/story?id=5759196 |work=ESPN.com |date=November 3, 2010 |language=en}} On January 2, 2013, Villanueva was fined $25,000 by the NBA for delivering a [[flagrant foul]] to [[Sacramento Kings]] guard [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]] the previous night. Villanueva had been ejected from the game for elbowing Thomas as Thomas drove to the basket. The NBA league office added the fine after reviewing the play.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/01/02/pistons-charlie-villanueva-fined/|title=Pistons' Villanueva fined $25K for flagrant foul|date=January 2, 2013|access-date=August 6, 2015|work=NBA.com}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2014–2016)=== On September 23, 2014, Villanueva signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite
